new_flaw.description: The new loop in reset keeps loading bitmap words downward until it finds any set bit. It does not stop once it passes endTick. When no initialized tick lies at or below the start tick, it loads every word down to int16.min, which is about 32,000 external reads, and the hook calls reset twice for each taxed swap.
new_flaw.scenario: Every position is above the current price, for example after the price fell below all ranges. The first taxed zero-for-one swap in a block runs this loop and runs out of gas, so the swap reverts. The post-hoc test for this case (forge_P7_posthoc.json) used about 148 million gas. In other layouts the gas grows with the distance to the next initialized tick below the start, not with the size of the swap.

claude-opus-5-5.reason: The loop only stops at a set bit or at int16.min, so with no initialized tick below the start it makes tens of thousands of bitmap reads, and the post-hoc test shows the swap needs about 148 million gas.

gpt-6.1-sol.reason: It reported no flaw, but the same loop ignores endTick and the out-of-gas case is real.

summary: Replaces the first _advanceToNextDown call with a loop that searches from the start tick's own bit and moves down one word at a time until it finds a set bit, then clamps the result to endTick. The ticks it returns are correct, but the loop does not stop once it passes endTick.
